## GET /admin-api/service-accounts

`getServiceAccounts`

**Every service account and the state of its rotation**

Every service account in this realm (#221) — a person entry carrying `stsServiceAccount` — paged in `accounts`, each with `username`, `owners` (each `{ dn, kind, name }`, #600), `destination`, `secretName`, `rotatedAt`, `previousPasswordUntil` (the overlap) and `rotation` (`rotates`, `nextDueAt`, `failures`, `lastError`, `lastAttemptAt`, `alarm`), and the realm's `policy` (`rotationEnabled`, `intervalDays`, `overlapMinutes`, `alarmFailures`, `from`) and `totals` (`accounts`, `withDestination`, `rotating`, `failing`, `alarms`). No password and no secret value is in the reply.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/service-accounts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `failing` | query | one of `true` |  | `true`: only accounts whose last rotation failed. |
| `account` | query | string |  | One service account, by username (#607): the answer is `{ found, account }` alone — `account` as a row of `accounts` is, with `ownerProtected` — and an owner of the account may ask it with owner:read. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/users

`getUsers`

**Everyone this service has authenticated, or one of them in full**

Without `user` it is the list. With it, one identity: the names they were seen under, how they authenticated each time, every sign-on session they hold with the tokens issued ON each of those, and their LDAP entry. A name this service has never seen answers 200 with `known: false` rather than 404 — it is an answer about the identity, not about the route.

The identity is a QUERY PARAMETER and not a path segment on purpose: the identities here contain the characters a path is made of (a Kerberos service principal is `HTTP/host`, a subject is a `urn:`), so /users/HTTP/web.example.com would be a two-segment path naming nobody.

ONE PAGE PARAMETER IS NOT IN THE LIST BELOW, because its name is data: each session's own token list is moved by `session-<the session id>Page`, so `?user=alice&session-8Qk3...Page=2` moves that block and no other, and each session in the reply answers with its own `tokensPaging`. It is named after the session rather than numbered so that the link still moves the same session after the list around it has changed, and it is paged at all because one browser session can hold most of the tokens this service remembers. OpenAPI cannot spell a parameter whose name is built at runtime, and a `session-{id}Page` in the list would generate a client that sends a literal `{id}` — so it is here in words instead.

**The ?user= reply's `authenticationEvents`** (#955) are the audit log's authentication attempts by this person, newest first, across every application and protocol: `authentication`, `authentication.refused`, `session.refuse` and `session.refused`. A row is this person's when its actor, the name they presented, `detail.sub` or `detail.presented` is their name, a name they have been seen under, or their subject, exactly as spelled. Each row is an audit event. `authenticationEventsMatched` is how many, `authenticationEventsPaging` pages them under `authenticationsPage`, `authenticationEventsKnownActors` says which actors have a user page, and `authenticationEventsLog` says how full the audit log is. The member is not `authentications`: that one is the count. The list holds no more history than the audit log does, and nothing in it is a credential. Another process's rows are read before this reply is built when `user` is set, the same wait GET /admin-api/audit makes.

THE LIST IS CAPPED AND THE COUNT IS NOT (#610). `directoryPeople` is how many people the realm's directory defines, counted by the directory without listing them (null where it offers no count). The rows are at most `scanLimit` of those people — `scanned` of them read, `capped` true when the directory held more — united with everybody this service has seen, so `known` is the length of that list and never the size of the directory. `directoryCounts` is what the page's tiles draw, over every person the directory defines, without listing them: `people`; `signedInHere`, those of them the register has seen authenticate (it keeps the most recent identities only), and `neverSignedInHere`, the rest; `withSecond`, `withTotp`, `withKeys`, `primaryKeys`, `unreadable`, `withPassword`, `passwordOnly` (a password and no second factor) and `noWayIn` (neither a password nor a sign-in key). Null where the directory offers no such count. `factors`, `authenticatedHere` and the `factor` filter stay the LIST's. A client comparing this resource with SCIM's `totalResults` reads `directoryPeople`, never `known` (#684).

THE COUNT HAS AN AGE (#684). `directoryCountedAt` is when this process's directory counted `directoryCounts` (ISO 8601), and `directoryCountsKeptFor` the most seconds it keeps that count against another process's committed writes — its own writes, and the ones it has applied, end it at once. Two requests answered by two workers inside that window may carry two figures. Both are null where the directory offers no count, and `directoryCountsKeptFor` is null where no other process can lag it (the directory in memory).

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/users` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | query | string |  | One identity, as the list's `key` names them. Returns the drill-down instead of the list. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of the identity key, case-insensitive. |
| `protocol` | query | string |  | Only identities that authenticated through this protocol family. The list's `protocols` member says which values there are; it is read off the data, so a family nobody has used is not offered. |
| `factor` | query | one of `any`, `totp`, `key`, `none`, `unreadable` |  | Only people holding a second factor of this kind, as on GET /admin-api/mfa. |
| `kind` | query | one of `service`, `person` |  | `service`: only service accounts (person entries carrying `stsServiceAccount`); `person`: everybody else. Each row says which in `serviceAccount`, and `serviceAccounts` counts them over the whole list. |
| `authenticationsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `authenticationEvents`, on the `?user=` reply only. Named rather than the bare `page` so it does not move the session list. The member is not `authentications`: that one is the count. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `sessionsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `sessions` to return, answered by `sessionsPaging`. Sign-on session blocks, which default to 5 rather than 50 because each one carries a token list of its own. Only the sessions ON this page are in the reply. |
| `tokensOnEndedSessionsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `tokensOnEndedSessions` to return, answered by `tokensOnEndedSessionsPaging`. Tokens issued on a session this service no longer holds. |
| `tokensWithNoSessionPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `tokensWithNoSession` to return, answered by `tokensWithNoSessionPaging`. Tokens issued with no browser session at all: the grants that never involve one. |
| `artifactsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `artifacts` to return, answered by `artifactsPaging`. SAML assertions, Kerberos tickets and credentials. |
| `federationLinksPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `federationLinks` to return, answered by `federationLinksPaging`. The federation partners' subjects linked to this person (#109), each `{ link, relationship, issuer, subject, relationshipExists }`. |
| `gnapGrantsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `gnapGrants` to return, answered by `gnapGrantsPaging`. The GNAP grants this person is the resource owner of (#432): each with its state, why it was finalized (`finalization.reason`: issued, revoked, rejected, expired), its rights, the tokens issued under it (label, format, expiry, state — never a value) and whether it can still be revoked, which POST /admin-api/gnap/revoke-grant does with `user`. `gnapGrantsCells` says what a multi-cell service's list leaves out. |
| `umaPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `uma` to return, answered by `umaPaging`. This person's UMA 2.0 (#1195): `resources` they own, the `shares` in their document, the permissions they hold in live RPTs (`held`, which POST /admin-api/uma/revoke-rpt revokes) and the requests waiting for them (`pending`). Null where UMA is not loaded. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/users/add-attribute

`addUserAttributeValue`

**Add a value to one of somebody's multi-valued attributes**

One attribute of the person's directory entry, written in place, as an `ldapmodify` of it would be. The attributes it takes are the person schema (person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson and the Identity Assurance claims) and the credential catalogue, less what is managed: `userPassword` (`set-password`), the binary ones, `uid`, `mail` (`set-mail`, which verifies it) and whichever attribute names the entry. `attributeEditor` in GET /admin-api/users?user= lists them, with what each holds and the shape its value must have. A change is told to Shared Signals as a SCIM or LDAP write of it is.

**`add`** appends `value`, and is refused on an attribute that holds one value (`displayName`, `employeeNumber`, `preferredLanguage`, `c`, `schacDateOfBirth`, and this service's own single-fact attributes) and for a value already held.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | string | yes | The attribute, as `attributeEditor.attributes[].name` in GET /admin-api/users?user= names it. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |
| `value` | string | yes | The value to add. |

**200**: The attribute and every value it now holds.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | string |  |  |
| `dn` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `mode` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `reason` | string |  |  |
| `values` | list |  |  |
| `values[]` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## POST /admin-api/users/add-certificate

`addUserCertificate`

**Store a certificate on somebody's entry, so an outside certificate authority's certificate signs them in**

Stores one X.509 certificate in the person's `userCertificate` (RFC 4523; written as `userCertificate;binary`). A certificate from an outside certificate authority — one trusted through the Client Truststores — is an identity at a door that reads a client certificate as a person (/tls/sign-in, the sign-in screen, SCIM, the XACML gates, Shared Signals, WS-Trust, LDAP SASL EXTERNAL) only while it is stored, byte for byte, on exactly one entry of the realm: never by its common name or subject (#1061). Refused when it is already stored on another entry (STS-ADMIN-0899) or the person has no entry (STS-ADMIN-0898). A renewed certificate is stored again.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificate` | string | yes | The leaf, as one PEM block or base64 DER. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: The certificates the entry stores now.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificates` | list |  |  |
| `certificates[].expired` | boolean |  |  |
| `certificates[].issuer` | string |  |  |
| `certificates[].notAfter` | string |  |  |
| `certificates[].notBefore` | string |  |  |
| `certificates[].readable` | boolean |  |  |
| `certificates[].serialNumber` | string |  |  |
| `certificates[].sha256` | string |  |  |
| `certificates[].subject` | string |  |  |
| `changed` | boolean |  |  |
| `dn` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `rule` | string |  |  |
| `sha256` | string |  |  |
| `user` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## GET /admin-api/users/app-passwords

`getUserAppPasswords`

**One person's app passwords, and which password-only doors refuse their own password**

Each app password the person holds — its public `id`, `name`, the `doors` it is accepted at, when it was made and by whom, and when and where it was last used. **Never the password and never its hash.** Beside them, `passwordOnlyDoors` says which of the five doors refuse this person's own password (in product mode, while they hold or must hold a second factor, less `authn.passwordAloneDoors`), and `doors` is the catalogue a scope is chosen from.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/users` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

`beginUserPasskeyEnrolment`

**Begin enrolling a passkey for somebody, in your own browser**

Mints a WebAuthn registration challenge bound to YOU (the access token's subject, which must be a person), the person and the lane, held for five minutes at most and usable once, and answers the ceremony your browser runs (`ceremony`): the challenge, the realm's RP ID, the PERSON's user handle (`user.id`, per lane, #643) with their name and display name (the passkey policy's userDisplayName), the credentials to exclude (the person's keys in that lane) and `options` — the algorithms offered in order and the realm's attestation, user verification, resident key, hints and timeout. Every byte string is base64url.

Refused unless the person's passkey policy's `adminEnrolment` is `on` (STS-AUTHN-0440, off by default), the person is in this realm's directory (STS-AUTHN-0441), the caller is a person (STS-AUTHN-0445), the realm accepts a passkey at all (STS-AUTHN-0531), and the lane and `webauthn.maxKeysPerPerson` allow it. No role is asked: a passkey has none since #1135, and the realm decides at each sign-in how it is used. There is no import of a registration made elsewhere.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `passkey`, `security-key` |  | Which kind of authenticator to ask for; the realm's attachment setting decides either way. |
| `lane` | one of `classical`, `pqc` |  | The lane (#643) where the realm offers both (webauthn.pqcAlongsideClassical); the classical one otherwise. |
| `role` | string |  | Ignored since #1135: a passkey has no role. Accepted so that an older body is not refused. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: `enrolmentId`, `expiresAt`, `lane`, `kind` and `ceremony`, or why it was not begun.

## POST /admin-api/users/clear-backup-codes

`clearUserBackupCodes`

**Clear somebody's recovery codes**

**THE ONLY ROUTE TO A SECOND SET.** A set is issued automatically, and ONCE, the first time somebody asks for one from the user portal; does nothing while a set exists, so clearing is what lets the next enrolment issue one.

**It cannot lock anybody out** — a recovery code is never a way in on its own — but it removes the way BACK, so somebody whose set is cleared and who then loses their phone needs an operator again.

**There is no operation that READS the codes and there will not be.** They are a working second factor; `GET /users` reports how many remain and never what they are. The person reads their own set back on `/portal/mfa`, which is the only place in this service that shows one.

Clearing a set nobody holds answers 400 rather than 200, for `clear-totp`'s reason.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence` | string |  | How the person's identity was verified, in at least 8 characters. Product mode requires it, and it is recorded in the audit log. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: Whose set was cleared. `sessionsEnded` counts the sessions a recovery code signed in, which were ended (#722); every other stays.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `problems` | list |  |  |

| `remaining` | number |  |  |
| `sessionsEnded` | number |  |  |
| `username` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## POST /admin-api/users/create

`createUser`

**Put a person in the directory before they authenticate**

An entry under `ou=users` usually appears because somebody AUTHENTICATED — at either sign-in screen, on a password grant, with a `UsernameToken`, in a Kerberos AS-REQ. This is how to get one in ahead of that, which is what a client testing claims from the directory needs: the entry carries the invented person behind that name, so a credential issued for them and an `ldapsearch` for the entry say the same thing from the start.

**One entry per person, and this is one of three doors onto that rule.** A username already here is refused with the DN that holds it — whatever protocol brought them, and whichever attribute their entry is named by, since a person whose entry was created by a client certificate is at `cn=<name>,ou=users` rather than `uid=<name>,ou=users`. An `ldapadd` under `ou=users` gets the same refusal as LDAP_ENTRY_ALREADY_EXISTS (68), because all three call one function.

**No password is set unless one is ASKED FOR** through `credential` below. That default is what this operation has always done and is right in development mode, where no password is checked here in this protocol or any other; in product mode a person with no credential cannot sign in, and `activation` is how they are given one. Creating the entry does not put the name in `GET /admin-api/users`: that lists identities this service has SEEN authenticate, and this writes what the directory HOLDS.

**SINCE 2026-09-06 IT TAKES THE PERSON'S DETAILS AND A CREDENTIAL**, which is what the console's /admin/users/new form posts. `attributes` are checked against the catalogue `GET /admin-api/users/new` publishes and an unknown name is REFUSED rather than dropped; `invent` decides whether the rest are made up, and it DEFAULTS TO TRUE so that a caller written before this gets exactly what it always got.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | object |  | What is known about them, as `{attribute: value}`. The names are the catalogue `GET /admin-api/users/new` publishes, in that document's own spelling, and they are the names the entry carries — so an `ldapsearch` shows exactly what was sent. **A NAME THAT IS NOT ON THE CATALOGUE IS REFUSED and the whole create fails**, rather than the value being ignored: silently dropping it would answer "created" to a request asking for something this did not do. `userPassword` is refused by that rule — use `credential` — and so is `uid`, which is `username`. An empty string is the same as sending nothing: the attribute is absent from the entry rather than present and empty. |
| `credential` | one of `none`, `password`, `generate`, `activation` |  | How they first get in. **`generate` is the DEFAULT since 2026-09-12**: a password drawn to satisfy this realm's password policy (`GET /admin-api/policies`), set, and RETURNED ONCE in `password` — this service stores a scrypt hash and cannot produce it again. It costs one hash per create, about 70ms, so a bulk load that wants nobody holding anything sends `none`. `none` was the default before, and in development mode it is enough to sign in, since no password is checked there; `password`, hashing the `password` field onto the entry, and refused by the password policy in product mode when it does not meet it; `activation`, issuing a single-use link and returning it ONCE in `activationUrl` for you to send them, at which they choose a password, a security key or both. **A CREDENTIAL STEP THAT FAILS DOES NOT UNDO THE CREATE.** A password can only be written onto an entry that exists, so the person is there either way; the reply is `ok: true` with `credentialError` set and says so, because answering `ok: false` would send a caller to create them again and meet "that username is taken". |
| `deliver` | one of `show`, `mail` |  | With `credential: activation`, `mail` (#63) sends the link to the address on the person's entry through the realm's mail transport and does NOT return it: the answer carries `mailedTo`. If it cannot be mailed the link is returned as with `show` (the default), with `mailError` saying why. |
| `destination` | string |  | With `serviceAccount`: the DN of the push destination (an application entry) its rotated password is written to. |
| `homeCell` | string |  | Only when this service is deployed as cells (#98): the id of the cell the person is homed in. Empty means the realm's `cells.homeCell`, or the cell that answers. Another cell's id makes the creation THERE; a cell the service does not have, or one in a jurisdiction the realm does not allow, is refused 400. Ignored in single-cell mode. |
| `invent` | boolean |  | Whether to MAKE UP the attributes not sent. **Defaults to TRUE**, which is what this operation has always done and what its own description above promises: `vc_claims.js` invents a consistent person per username, so the entry and any credential issued for them agree from the start. Send `false` for an entry carrying ONLY what you sent — its object classes, its uid, a description and your attributes. That is what the console's form does. It is not a promise the entry stays that way: the Populate button on /admin/vc fills every missing SELECTED attribute on every person, and does not know which were typed. |
| `note` | string |  | Optional. What the entry's `description` says about why it exists; the default says it was created by hand rather than by authenticating. An `attributes.description` wins over it, because an operator's own sentence about a person is the more useful one and two values would be the entry answering the question twice. |
| `owners` | list |  | With `serviceAccount`: the people and groups answerable for it (#600) — each a DN, a username or a group's cn; an array, or a string of one per line. At least one while the policy's `requireOwner` is on (the default). |
| `owners[]` | string |  |  |
| `password` | string |  | Read only when `credential` is `password`. Hashed with scrypt by credentials.js and never stored or logged in the clear; nothing in this service can show it again. |
| `passwordConfirm` | string |  | Optional, and CHECKED WHERE SENT: the console's form always sends it, because a mistyped password nobody can read back is a person who cannot sign in and nobody who can say why. An API caller with one value has nothing to mistype against and may omit it. |
| `secretName` | string |  | With `destination`: the secret's name or path there, which must already exist. |
| `serviceAccount` | boolean |  | Create the person as a SERVICE ACCOUNT (#221): a person entry carrying `stsServiceAccount`, governed by the realm's service-account policy. `owners`, and `destination` with `secretName`, are read with it, and checked BEFORE the person is created — a refusal creates nobody. |
| `username` | string | yes | The name they will authenticate under — the same string that appears in a token's `sub` and on /admin/users. Not a DN and not a `did:`, and it may not carry a character RFC 4514 reserves in a DN: those name entries that get here by being presented rather than by being created. |

**200**: The entry as created, in `entry`, with its `dn`; `typed` naming the attributes you sent and `invented` whether the rest were made up. A generated password is in `password` and an activation link in `activationUrl` — EACH RETURNED ONCE, because what is stored is a hash and this service cannot produce either again.

## POST /admin-api/users/create-app-password

`createUserAppPassword`

**Make an app password for somebody, returned once**

Generates an APP PASSWORD for the person — twenty-four characters, printed in groups of four — names it, scopes it to one or more of the five password-only doors (`ldap`, `wstrust`, `scim`, `ssf`, `est`), stores a scrypt hash of it on their entry and **returns it ONCE** in `appPassword`. Nothing can show it again.

**What it is for**: in product mode a person who holds a second factor, or of whom one is required, is refused their own password at those five doors, which cannot ask for the second factor; an app password scoped to a door is accepted there instead. It is ONE factor, it is accepted ONLY at the doors it names, and NEVER at the sign-in screen or any browser sign-in. A disabled account refuses it; a password reset leaves it alone.

**Shared Signals**: a CAEP `credential-change` (`password`, `create`) with its name as `friendly_name`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doors` | list | yes | The doors it is accepted at. At least one. |
| `doors[]` | one of `ldap`, `wstrust`, `scim`, `ssf`, `est` |  |  |
| `name` | string | yes | What it is for — the client it goes in. At most 64 characters, unique among this person's. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: The app password ONCE (`appPassword`), its public four-character `id`, name, doors and when it was made.

## POST /admin-api/users/deactivate-published-did

`deactivateUserPublishedDid`

**Deactivate a did:web this realm publishes for somebody**

Deactivates one of the person's published DIDs (#1291): its address answers 410 Gone with `{ id, deactivated: true }` for good, a resolver reports `deactivated: true`, its version history stays resolvable, and it no longer signs the person in, nor is it preferred or released in the `did` claim. A deactivated DID is never reactivated. An administrator never creates or changes one: that is the person's act on /portal/self-issued. A DID the person does not hold, or one already deactivated, is refused (STS-VC-0172).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/users/disable

`disableUserAccount`

**Disable somebody's account, and end everything they hold**

Sets `pwdAccountLockedTime` (draft-behera-ldap-password-policy's administrative lock, `000001010000Z`) on the person's entry. From then on EVERY door refuses them, in every mode: a password anywhere (the sign-in screen, an LDAP bind, the password grant, WS-Trust, SCIM and SSF Basic, EST), a session from any sign-in (a security key, federation, SPNEGO, a TLS client certificate, the wallet), a Kerberos AS-REQ (KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED), every token grant made on their behalf (`invalid_grant`, a refresh token included), every assertion, and this API.

**Everything they hold is ended at once**, by the same global logout `POST /admin-api/logout/global` performs: sessions (with CAEP `session-revoked` and back-channel Logout Tokens to their relying parties), tokens, codes, directory connections and Kerberos tickets. RISC receivers are sent `account-disabled`. Front-channel notifications need the person's own browser and are not sent. SCIM's `active: false` is the same act.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string |  | Recorded on the audit row. |
| `riscReason` | one of `hijacking`, `bulk-account` |  | RISC account-disabled's `reason` (section 2.2), sent to receivers; omitted when not given (#146). |

## POST /admin-api/users/disable-mfa

`disableUserSecondFactors`

**Remove every second factor somebody holds**

Removes the authenticator app enrolment, every passkey and the recovery codes, in one act. Until #1135 it took only the keys enrolled in the `mfa` role; a passkey has no role since, and any of them may answer the second step, so it takes all of them. **Refused where the passkeys are their way in** (STS-AUTHN-0161): a person with no password, in a realm where a passkey may be a first factor, who holds one. Reset their password or issue a reset link first. If a second factor is still REQUIRED of the person — `require-mfa`, or the realm's authentication policy — their next sign-in asks them to enrol a new one, which is how to reset somebody's MFA.

Refused for somebody who holds no second factor.

**Shared Signals**: a CAEP `credential-change` (`delete`) for the authenticator app (`app`) and for each key (`fido2-roaming`), and a RISC `recovery-information-changed` where recovery codes were removed.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence` | string |  | How the person's identity was verified, in at least 8 characters. Product mode requires it, and it is recorded in the audit log. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: What was removed, and whether a second factor is still required of them (`requirement`). `sessionsEnded` counts the sessions each removed factor signed in, which were ended (#963); every other stays.

## POST /admin-api/users/enrol-self-issued-subject

`enrolUserSelfIssuedSubject`

**Enrol a self-issued (SIOPv2) subject for somebody**

Enrols a did:jwk, did:key or did:web, an RFC 9278 JWK thumbprint URI, a base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint or a public JWK (as JSON) on the person's entry. A self-issued ID Token signed by that key then signs them in, while oid4vp.signInSelfIssued is on. Refused where the subject is already enrolled for anybody in the realm. A person enrols their own on /portal/self-issued by proving the key with their wallet.

What this enrols is recorded as BY VALUE (`proof: admin`, unproven), and nothing that releases or binds a subject reads it. A did:web's DID document is fetched now and every authentication key it names is pinned; a later sign-in with any other key is refused (STS-VC-0126). A document that cannot be fetched or names no such key is refused (STS-ADMIN-0871) (#693).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| `label` | string |  | A name for it, at most 64 characters. |
| `subject` | string | yes | The DID, thumbprint or JWK. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |

## POST /admin-api/users/export-ldif

`exportUserLdif`

**Export one person's entry as an LDIF file**

Answers the person's directory entry as an RFC 2849 LDIF document with one record: `ldif` (the text) and `files` (the same, named and base64, which the console saves). The attributes a create takes only — the inetOrgPerson attributes, the credential catalogue's and the realm's custom attributes, which is what `import-ldif` writes back; nothing this service recorded about the person (sign-in methods, federation sightings, consents, flags), no group membership and no `entryUUID`. The DN is the entry's own; `import-ldif` creates the person in whichever realm it is called in.

**CREDENTIAL MATERIAL IS LEFT OUT BY DEFAULT** and named in `leftOut`. With `credentials` true the password's stored hash, the authenticator app (its secret opened), the passkeys and their user handles, the recovery codes, the app passwords, the stored client certificates, the HOBA keys and the CIBA user code's hash are written **UNENCRYPTED**: a value sealed under this process's key-encryption key is opened, because a file sealed under it opens nowhere else. Keep such a file as you would the secrets in it. Kerberos keys, the RFC 7523 and RFC 7522 key pairs, enrolled certificates and enrolment secrets are never exported: each is minted by its own subsystem. An audit row (`user.export`) says whether credentials went with the file, never a value. Asked for a recent sign-in, as `set-password` is.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `credentials` | boolean, or one of `true`, `false`, `on` |  | Include credential material, UNENCRYPTED. False when absent. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: `ldif`, `files` (one `.ldif`), the `attributes` written, `credentials`, and `leftOut`: the credential attributes not written.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list |  |  |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `changed` | boolean |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/users/federation-link

`linkUserFederation`

**Link a federation partner's subject to a person**

Adds a `federationLink` — `<relationship> <issuer> <subject>` — to the person's entry, so that the partner of that service-provider-side relationship signs them in when it asserts that subject. The subject is the partner's STABLE identifier for them (OpenID Connect `sub`, a SAML persistent NameID), never a name or an address, and the issuer is the relationship's `fedPeer` when omitted. Refused when another person already carries the link (a subject names one person), for a relationship that is not service-provider side, or for a subject that cannot be written. A console administrator is still refused at the sign-in unless the relationship sets `fedMayAssertAdministrators`. The person's links are `federationLinks` (paged by `federationLinksPage`) on `GET /admin-api/users?user=`, and a relationship's are `links` on `GET /admin-api/federation?relationship=`. SCIM sets the same values through the `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:iya-sts:2.0:User` extension.

## POST /admin-api/users/import-ldif

`importUserLdif`

**Create a person from an LDIF file**

Reads an RFC 2849 LDIF document holding ONE person's record, as `export-ldif` writes it (`uid=<name>,ou=users,…` with that name as its one `uid`), and creates that person in the realm this is called in, through the create `POST /admin-api/users/create` makes: the realm's attribute policy, the username rules and one entry per person are its checks. **IT NEVER OVERWRITES**: a username already here is refused, naming the entry that holds it (STS-LDAP-0218). A new `entryUUID`, and so a new subject, is minted; a file carrying one is refused.

Only the attributes a create takes and the credentials an export writes are taken; a record carrying what this service records about a person, or a credential a subsystem mints, is refused naming each (STS-LDAP-0219). A credential in the file is written as stored: a password only as the hash this service writes (a hash cannot be held to the password policy, so a clear password is refused — set one with `set-password` after the import), the authenticator secret and a legacy recovery-code set sealed again wherever the key-encryption key persists, a passkey user handle or a stored certificate refused when somebody here holds it already (STS-LDAP-0220). **No Kerberos key is derived from a hash**: the person has none until their password is set again. A CAEP credential-change is sent for each kind of credential that came in, and the import is audited (`user.import`) with the attribute names, never a value. Give the document as `ldif` (its text), or as `file` (its name and text), which is how the console sends an uploaded file. Asked for a recent sign-in, as `set-password` is.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

**200**: The `username` created, its `dn`, the `attributes` the create wrote and the `credentials` written after it.

## POST /admin-api/users/issue-activation

`issueActivationLink`

**Issue a one-time activation link for a provisioned person**

How somebody created through POST /admin-api/users/create, SCIM or an LDAP add comes to have a way in. They are provisioned with no credential; this mints a single-use, time-limited URL at which they choose a password, a security key, or both.

**THE URL IS RETURNED ONCE AND NEVER AGAIN.** What is stored is a scrypt hash, so this service cannot produce it a second time — only replace it, which is what calling this again does. Treat it as the credential it is: anybody holding it can complete the account setup, so a leaked link is an account takeover.

It expires after `security.activationTtlMinutes` and is spent the moment the setup FINISHES — not when the link is opened, because a link burned by a mail scanner or a browser prefetch would strand the person it was for.

There is deliberately no self-service version: until the account is activated nobody has proved the address on it is theirs. `deliver: "mail"` (#63) has this service mail it instead of returning it.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deliver` | one of `show`, `mail` |  | `mail` (#63) sends the link to the address on the person's entry through the realm's mail transport and does NOT return it: the answer carries `mailedTo`. If it cannot be mailed the link is returned as with `show` (the default), with `mailError` saying why. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. They must already exist. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: The activation URL, ONCE, and when it expires — or, with `deliver: "mail"`, the address it was mailed to.

## POST /admin-api/users/issue-password-reset

`issuePasswordResetLink`

**Revoke somebody's password and issue a one-time reset link**

Mints a single-use link to `/portal/reset-password`, **returned ONCE** in `resetUrl` (absolute, on the address this request arrived at, realm prefix included), valid for `security.passwordResetTtlMinutes`. The token in it is stored as a hash; issuing another replaces it.

**The password the person had is REMOVED** and they are **signed out of everything**, so until the link is used they cannot sign in with a password. At the link they choose a new one under the realm's password policy; the removed password is in the history, so it cannot simply be chosen again where the history is enforced.

**Shared Signals**: a CAEP `credential-change` (`password`, `revoke`) where a password was removed, a RISC `account-credential-change-required` and `recovery-activated` (#146), RISC `credential-compromise` when `compromised` is true, and a CAEP `credential-change` (`password`, `create`) when the link is spent.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

| `deliver` | one of `show`, `mail` |  | `mail` (#63) sends the link to the address on the person's entry through the realm's mail transport and does NOT return it: the answer carries `mailedTo`. If it cannot be mailed the link is returned as with `show` (the default), with `mailError` saying why. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

## POST /admin-api/users/issue-signing-certificate

`issueUserSigningCertificate`

**Issue somebody a message-signing certificate from this realm's CA**

Generates a key pair and certifies it from the realm's `message-signing` Issuing CA with `digitalSignature` only and `urn:sts:person:<username>` as its subjectAltName. A WS-Trust request whose WS-Security signature over the SOAP Body and Timestamp verifies under it authenticates the person as its requester; it signs nobody in over TLS. An administrator's act: the person has no door to it on the user portal (#521).

**THIS REPLY IS THE ONLY COPY OF THE PRIVATE KEY.** `files` holds a PKCS#12 (base64), an encrypted PKCS#8 PEM key and the PEM chain, all protected by `password`, which is neither stored nor audited. Refused past `pki.messageSigningCertificateMax` valid certificates (`STS-PKI-0220`), for a person with no entry (`STS-ADMIN-0905`), for a key algorithm outside `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `ec-p256`, `ec-p384`, and in a realm with no certificate authority.

## GET /admin-api/users/new

`getNewUserForm`

**Every attribute a person may be created with, and the four ways they can be given a way in**

The ATTRIBUTE CATALOGUE a create takes in `attributes` — one row per attribute a person in this directory may carry, each naming the claim it reaches in an issued token or credential and the document its name comes from — plus the container DN the entry would land in, the realm, and the four `credential` options.

**It creates nobody**: the create is `POST /admin-api/users/create`. This is the list that call validates against, and an attribute name that is not on it is REFUSED rather than dropped — so a caller that reads this first cannot be told afterwards that half of what it sent was ignored.

**`uid` and `userPassword` are deliberately not on it.** `uid` is the username, sent as `username`, and a second way to set it would allow an entry at `uid=alice` whose uid attribute says `bob`. A password goes through `credential`, so that `credentials.js` hashes it — an attribute door that took `userPassword` would write one in the clear.

**The container is THIS REALM'S.** The embedded directory is per trust realm, so `/realm/acme/admin-api/users/new` answers with acme's `ou=users` and a person created there is invisible to every other realm.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/users/new` on the admin console.

It creates nobody. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |

## GET /admin-api/users/published-dids

`getUserPublishedDids`

**The did:web DIDs this realm publishes for one person**

Each did:web this realm publishes for the person (#1291): its random id (`rid`), the DID, where its document is (`documentUrl`), who holds its key (`custody`: `wallet`, `realm` or `download`), its `state` (`active`, `deactivated`, or `suspended` while the account is disabled), the provenance of its self-issued subject (`proof`), whether it is the preferred DID, its `currentVersion`, any change waiting for its new key (`pending`), and every version with its keys (ids and algorithms, never a private key) and what authorized it. Beside them, whether the realm publishes DIDs now (`did.personPublishing`), its custody and how many active ones a person may hold. An administrator may deactivate one (`deactivate-published-did`) and never create or change one.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/users` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/users/record-verification

`recordUserVerification`

**Record an identity verification for somebody**

Keeps an OpenID Connect for Identity Assurance 1.0 `verification` element on the person's entry, with the claims it covered. `trust_framework` must be one of oauth2.idaTrustFrameworks; each evidence element is checked by its type (document, electronic_record, vouch, electronic_signature) against the vocabularies discovery publishes; `time` defaults to now. Each claim's value is taken from the entry as it is now, and a claim the entry holds nothing for is refused. The console's form posts the same thing as flat fields.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claims` | list | yes | The claims it covered, from claims_in_verified_claims_supported. |

## POST /admin-api/users/remove-attribute

`removeUserAttributeValue`

**Remove one value from one of somebody's attributes**

One attribute of the person's directory entry, written in place, as an `ldapmodify` of it would be. The attributes it takes are the person schema (person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson and the Identity Assurance claims) and the credential catalogue, less what is managed: `userPassword` (`set-password`), the binary ones, `uid`, `mail` (`set-mail`, which verifies it) and whichever attribute names the entry. `attributeEditor` in GET /admin-api/users?user= lists them, with what each holds and the shape its value must have. A change is told to Shared Signals as a SCIM or LDAP write of it is.

**`remove`** takes off the value named, compared without regard to case; it is refused for a value not held and for the last value of `cn` or `sn`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | string | yes | The attribute, as `attributeEditor.attributes[].name` in GET /admin-api/users?user= names it. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |
| `value` | string | yes | The value to remove. |

**200**: The attribute and every value it now holds.

## POST /admin-api/users/rename-key

`renameUserPasskey`

**Rename one of somebody's passkeys**

Goes through the same `renameKey()` the person's own portal calls (`POST /portal/rename-key`): a name is at most 60 characters with no control characters, and an EMPTY name restores the default — the provider FIDO MDS names for the key's AAGUID where a BLOB is loaded, else the credential manager's, else "Passkey" or "Security key". The credential id is the base64url one on this person's `factors.keys`. Audited; no Shared Signals event, because a name says nothing about what the key proves.

## POST /admin-api/users/require-mfa

`requireUserSecondFactor`

**Require somebody to sign in with a second factor**

Sets `stsMfaRequired` on the person's entry. At the sign-in screen they are then asked for a second factor — and, while they hold none, shown a step to enrol an authenticator app or a passkey before any session is started. A passwordless passkey sign-in is refused while it is required.

In product mode it also refuses their own password at the five password-only doors — an LDAP bind, a WS-Trust UsernameToken, SCIM, SSF and EST Basic — answered as a wrong password; an app password (`create-app-password`) is what they use there (#101). In product the KDC refuses their password alone too (KDC_ERR_POLICY, #173); a ticket takes an authenticator code through FAST and OTP, or a certificate through PKINIT (#179). **What it does not reach** is a sign-in that is neither that screen nor one of those doors: federation, a TLS client certificate. The authentication policy's `requireSecondFactor: always` is the same requirement for every person in the realm.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

|---|---|---|---|

| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

`resetUserPassword`

**Reset somebody's password to a generated one, returned once**

Generates a password under this realm's password policy, sets it, and **returns it ONCE** in `password` — the entry holds a scrypt hash and nothing can show it again. Then three things the ordinary `set-password` does not do: `pwdReset` is set, so the person must choose their own password at the sign-in screen before anything is signed in; any password reset link outstanding is spent; and they are **signed out of everything** through the same function `POST /admin-api/logout/global` calls.

**Shared Signals**: a CAEP `credential-change` (`password`, `update`) and a RISC `account-credential-change-required`, plus a CAEP `session-revoked` for each session the sign-out ends. They are sent after the reply, and `caep.autoEmitTypes` and `risc.autoEmitTypes` decide whether they go at all.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compromised` | boolean |  | The reset is BECAUSE a credential was compromised: RISC `credential-compromise` (`password`) is sent as well (#146). |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

## POST /admin-api/users/rotate-password

`rotateServiceAccountPassword`

**Rotate a service account's password now**

QUEUES a rotation of the service account's password on the scheduler's leader (the job `service-accounts.rotate-now`, #221): a password drawn by the password policy's generator at the service-account policy's length is PUSHED to the account's destination first and committed here only once the push succeeded; the previous password is accepted for the policy's overlap. A failed push changes nothing. The answer is the run's id — `GET /admin-api/scheduler` shows its outcome — and never a password: the destination is where it is read.

Refused for an entry that is not a service account, or one that names no destination. A rotating account's password cannot be set by hand (`set-password`, `reset-password`): this is the way.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | string | yes | The service account, as /admin-api/users names it. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: The queued run (`runId`, `alreadyQueued`).

## POST /admin-api/users/set-attribute

`setUserAttribute`

**Replace every value of one of somebody's attributes**

One attribute of the person's directory entry, written in place, as an `ldapmodify` of it would be. The attributes it takes are the person schema (person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson and the Identity Assurance claims) and the credential catalogue, less what is managed: `userPassword` (`set-password`), the binary ones, `uid`, `mail` (`set-mail`, which verifies it) and whichever attribute names the entry. `attributeEditor` in GET /admin-api/users?user= lists them, with what each holds and the shape its value must have. A change is told to Shared Signals as a SCIM or LDAP write of it is.

**`set` REPLACES** every value with `value`; an empty `value` removes the attribute, except `cn` and `sn`, which every person must hold.

## POST /admin-api/users/set-delegation-semantics

`setUserDelegationSemantics`

**Set the delegation semantics a person allows**

Writes `stsDelegationSemantics` (the semantics the person allows: `delegation`, `impersonation`, or both; empty leaves it to the issuance policy, which reads an empty set as both for a subject and delegation only for an actor) and `stsDefaultDelegationSemantics` (what an act they are part of is when the request does not say). Read by the exchange policy at an RFC 8693 token exchange, a WS-Trust OnBehalfOf / ActAs and a Kerberos S4U request (#186).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |

## POST /admin-api/users/set-password

`setUserPassword`

**Set or replace somebody's password**

Hashed with scrypt by `credentials.js`, which is the one place in this service a password is ever verified or set, and written to `userPassword` on their directory entry. **It cannot be read back by anything** — not this API, not the console, not an `ldapsearch`, which sees the hash — so a lost password is replaced rather than recovered.

Send `password`, or `generate: true` to have one made up and RETURNED ONCE. The person must already exist; this creates nobody.

**IN DEVELOPMENT MODE THIS CHANGES ALMOST NOTHING AND IS STILL WORTH DOING.** Nothing here checks a password in development — every one is accepted — so setting one does not make a sign-in work that would otherwise fail. What it does is put the attribute on the entry, which is what an LDAP client reads, what `hasPassword()` counts, and what product mode would need. In PRODUCT mode it is the credential.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate` | boolean |  | Make one up instead — 32 bytes of randomBytes, base64url, the same generator the product-mode bootstrap account uses. It is RETURNED ONCE in `password` and never again. |
| `password` | string |  | The password to set. Required unless `generate` is true. |
| `passwordConfirm` | string |  | Optional, checked where sent. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. They must already exist. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: Whether it was set, and — only where it was GENERATED — the password, once. A password you sent is never echoed back: you already hold it, and returning it would put it in a second place.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |

| `password` | string |  |  |

`setUserPreferredSelfIssuedSubject`

Marks the subject — a DID the person PROVED with their wallet (`proof: wallet`) — as their preferred DID, and clears the mark from every other; an empty `subject` clears it. ## POST /admin-api/users/set-service-account

`setUserServiceAccount`

**Make somebody a service account, or a person again**

A service account is a PERSON entry carrying `stsServiceAccount` (#221): everything a person is — a password, app passwords, Kerberos keys, groups, roles, Shared Signals under their `iss_sub` — and governed by the realm's service-account policy (`GET /admin-api/policies`, kind `serviceAccount`): whether the second factor is exempt, whether a browser sign-in is allowed (not by default), which password doors open, and whether its password rotates and is pushed to a secrets manager.

`serviceAccount` true (the default) sets or changes it: `owners`, the WHOLE list of the people and groups in this realm who answer for it (#600) — it replaces the list the account names, at most 25, at least one while the policy's `requireOwner` is on; `destination`, a push destination's DN, and `secretName` go together. `serviceAccount` false makes them an ordinary person again and clears the owner, the destination and the rotation state.

Where the policy refuses a service account every browser sign-in, becoming one ENDS the person's sessions (`signedOut`). SCIM does not carry the flag; an LDAP modify by a holder of Admin Write may, under the same rules.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | string |  | The DN of the push destination (an application entry). |
| `owners` | list |  | The people and groups answerable for the account (#600), each a DN, a username or a group's cn: an array, or a string of one per line. It REPLACES the owners the account names; absent or empty is none, refused while the policy requires an owner. |
| `owners[]` | string |  |  |
| `secretName` | string |  | The secret's name or path at the destination; it must already exist there. |
| `serviceAccount` | boolean |  | true makes or keeps them a service account (the default); false makes them a person again. |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

## POST /admin-api/users/stop-requiring-mfa

`stopRequiringUserSecondFactor`

## POST /admin-api/users/update-fields

`updateUserFields`

**Set several of somebody's attributes at once**

What the Save button of a tab of a person's Attributes on the console does. Each member of `fields` names an attribute `attributeEditor` in GET /admin-api/users?user= lists as editable, and gives what it should hold: a single-valued attribute is SET (an empty string or array clears it), and a multi-valued one has the values put in added and then the values taken out removed — exactly `set-attribute`, `add-attribute` and `remove-attribute`, applied per attribute, so every rule those hold still holds, and each change is audited and told to Shared Signals as one of those is. An attribute whose values did not change is not written.

What one attribute refuses does not undo another: the reply names what was saved (`changed`) and every refusal, and answers 400 when there was any.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/users, POST /admin/users/new, POST /admin/users/edit and POST /admin/users/service-account` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | object |  | Attribute name to a string or an array of strings; empty clears it. |
| `present` | list |  | The fields the console's form drew, by attribute name, space or comma separated or as a list: each one is cleared when the form carries no value for it. |
| `present[]` | string |  |  |
| `user` | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `username` | string |  | Accepted for `user`. |

**200**: The attributes saved (`changed`).

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changed` | list |  |  |
| `changed[]` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `user` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changed` | list |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/users/verifications

`getUserVerifications`

**One person's identity verifications (OpenID Connect for Identity Assurance)**

Each verification recorded for the person, newest first: its `id`, where it came from (`source`: admin, wallet or certificate), when and by whom, the `verification` element — trust framework, time, evidence — and the `claims` it covered with the values that were verified. A client's `verified_claims` request is answered from these, for a claim only while the entry still holds the verified value. Beside them, the vocabularies a record is made from.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/users` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | query | string |  | The older spelling of `user`, read when `user` is absent. |
| `user` | query | string | yes | The person, as /admin-api/users names them. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |
